name: – Dariusz Joński – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the accession of Tuvalu to the Interim Partnership Agreement between the European Community, of the one part, and the Pacific States, of the other part
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees that Tuvalu should join a trade agreement between the EU and several Pacific countries. Tuvalu is about to lose special free access to the EU market because it is no longer classified as one of the world's poorest countries. Joining this agreement lets Tuvalu keep selling goods to the EU without duties or quotas. Parliament's consent is needed before this can happen.

- Tuvalu joins the EU's trade agreement with Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Samoa and Solomon Islands.
- Tuvalu's exporters keep duty-free, quota-free access to the EU market.
- Parliament has given its consent; the Council must now adopt the decision.
